title: Settings
dialogDescription: Manage MailX language, appearance, notifications, sending and security.
recoveredDescription: Default settings are in use. The original file was preserved as settings.json.bak.
mailDarkModeDescription: Some messages look better on a white background.
fontHint: Separate multiple font names with commas.
fontError: Font names contain unsupported characters or exceed the allowed length or count.
remoteImagesDescription: Loading images may let the sender know you read the message.
avatarsDescription: Online lookup is required. The lookup service can learn whose messages you receive.
senderAccountDescription: When writing from a mailbox folder, use that account. From All inboxes, use the account selected here, or the first account added when following the current mailbox. Replies and forwards always use the original message’s account.
undoDescription: After confirming send, the message waits for this period. Undo from the notification to return to the composer. Turn this off to send immediately.
testNotificationHint: If no notification appears, allow MailX notifications in system settings.
autostartHint: Start MailX automatically when you sign in to this computer.
silentStartHint: Run in the background at login. Opening MailX yourself still shows the main window. The window appears if no background entry is available.
autostartUnavailable: Configure launch at login in an installed copy of MailX.
autostartReadFailed: Could not read launch at login status
autostartSaveFailed: Could not change launch at login
autostartUnknown: The current status could not be confirmed.
autostartSystemError: Could not read or change the startup entry. Check system permissions and login startup settings, then try again.
languageHint: The language used for the app interface.
closeBehaviorHint: Applies only to closing the main window. The minimize button keeps its system behavior.
closePromptTitle: What should happen when you close MailX?
closePromptDescription: If you keep MailX running, it will continue syncing mail, sending messages you confirmed, and receiving notifications. Reopen it from the system tray or app shortcut.
closePromptMacDescription: If you keep MailX running, it will continue syncing mail, sending messages you confirmed, and receiving notifications. Reopen the window from the Dock. Other compose windows stay open.
rememberCloseChoice: Remember my choice and do not ask again
trayUnavailable: The system tray is currently unavailable, so MailX cannot hide the window and keep running. Cancel to keep the window open, or quit the app. Your saved close preference will not change automatically.
showMenuBarIcon: Show MailX in the menu bar
showMenuBarIconHint: Adds shortcuts to open windows and quit. Hiding the icon does not stop background activity.
quitMailxHint: Save drafts and stop background mail activity until you open MailX again.
quitting: Saving drafts and waiting for sending to finish…
quitTimedOut: Quit was cancelled because drafts have not finished saving or mail is still sending. Check the compose windows or try quitting again later.
quitSaveFailedTitle: Could not finish saving before quitting
quitSaveFailedDescription: MailX has not confirmed the quit. Resolve the save error and try again. Unsaved layout changes are kept for the next save attempt.

mcpFailure.endpointInUse: The local endpoint is already in use; another MailX may be running
mcpFailure.endpointCreateFailed: The local endpoint could not be created
mcpFailure.permissionDenied: The system denied access to the endpoint or its folder
mcpFailure.discoveryWriteFailed: The connection info file could not be written
mcpFailure.tokenUnavailable: A secure token could not be generated

mcpClientsHint: Copy the configuration and paste it into your MCP client.
mcpCopyFailed: Could not copy the client configuration
mcpToggleFailed: Could not change the MCP server setting
mcpConfirmAccess: External programs can read mail and drafts from all accounts, create, edit and delete drafts, manage attachments, and send mail without per-message confirmation.
mcpConfirmLimits: MailX attempts to sync read and starred flags to the server; archiving stays on this device. Mail cannot be deleted.
mcpConfirmLocal: Programs running as your system user can connect and read local files to attach.
mcpConfirmOff: You can turn it off here at any time.
